current.text: Mitchell Robinson is gone and Andre Drummond replaces him. The Knicks' big-man depth is very thin, with only Towns and Drummond, and they will likely sign just one more big.
He is a projected starter with Brunson, Bridges, Hart and Anunoby. The team is expected to use few double-big lineups.
Without Mitchell Robinson next to him, experts expect some of his rebounds, scoring, FG% and blocks to come back.
He is the best fantasy player on the Knicks.
Experts think he is unlikely to get back to 35 minutes and 24 points a game. He is projected at about 31 minutes under Mike Brown.
The Knicks won the championship after a long Finals run.

Experts disagree on early-season rest. Earlier previews expected the Knicks to trim his minutes and rest him more on back-to-backs over the first 30 or so games after the Finals run. The newest preview says a weaker team in a stronger East may not be able to rest players as much.
Experts call his Yahoo rank of 16 reasonable for categories. Taking him at pick 13 is debatable, and getting him at pick 22 is good value.
In an expert auction mock he was valued at 30 USD or more and went for 36 USD.
The Knicks are projected to win about 50 to 54 games.
The Knicks have a weak fantasy playoff schedule for a season ending March 28. They play a league-minimum 13 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He has a history of knee, lower leg and other lower-body injuries.
He showed some signs of declining athleticism in the regular season but looked good in the playoffs.
Rebounds are his standout category and a real outlier against the whole player pool.
He gives a high FT% on solid volume and makes threes at a good rate for a big man.
Turnovers are his weakest category and are high for a frontcourt player.

note: Expect to pay around 40 USD. Yahoo values him at 41 USD with an average cost of 43.8 USD, ESPN has him at 37 USD, an expert mock sold him for 36 USD, and he cost 46 USD in our league last year, so anything near the high 30s is fair value for a rank 16 to 21 player. He fits any build that wants rebounds, FT% from a big and some threes from the frontcourt, and he fits punt TO best. His weak playoff schedule for our March 28 end lowers his value a little. Early in the season, check whether he plays more than about 31 minutes, whether the Knicks rest him after the Finals run, and whether his rebounds and FG% go up without Mitchell Robinson.
